readings.title: The Demise of Aḥaz
readings.subtitle: The conclusion of a structurally unfit reign.
readings.text: [2 Kings 16:19] And the rest of the acts of Aḥaz which he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? [20] So Aḥaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ. And Ḥizqiyahu his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: Excluded from the Royal Burial-Sites
readings.subtitle: Aḥaz is buried, but denied the honor of the sovereigns.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 28:26] And the rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, see, they are written in the book of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah and Yisra’ěl. [27] So Aḥaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Yerushalayim, but they did not bring him into the burial-sites of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl. And Ḥizqiyahu his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: The Muster Against Baḇel
readings.subtitle: Gathering the weapons of displeasure against the epicenter of confusion.
readings.text: [Isaiah 13:1] The message concerning Baḇel which Yeshayahu son of Amots saw. [2] <dq>“Lift up a banner on the high mountain, raise your voice to them; wave your hand, let them enter the gates of the nobles.</dq> [3] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have commanded <dn>My</dn> set-apart ones; <dn>I</dn> have also called <dn>My</dn> mighty men for <dn>My</dn> displeasure, <dn>My</dn> proudly exulting ones.”</dq> [4] The noise of an uproar in the mountains, like that of many people! A noise of uproar of the reigns of nations gathered together! <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is gathering an army for battle. [5] They are coming from a distant land, from the end of the heavens, even <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>His</dn> weapons of displeasure, to destroy all the earth.

readings.title: The Terror of the Coming Day
readings.subtitle: The approaching absolute justice melts the hearts of men.
readings.text: [Isaiah 13:6] Howl, for the day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is near! It comes as a destruction from the Almighty. [7] Therefore all hands go limp, every man’s heart melts, [8] and they shall be afraid. Pangs and sorrows take hold of them, they are in pain as a woman in labour; they are amazed at one another, their faces aflame!

readings.title: Cosmic Shake and Strict Tsedek
readings.subtitle: The physical universe responds to the extraction of what is rightfully due.
readings.text: [Isaiah 13:9] See, the day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is coming, fierce, with wrath and heat of displeasure, to lay the earth waste, and destroy its sinners from it. [10] For the stars of the heavens and their constellations do not give off their light. The sun shall be dark at its rising, and the moon not send out its light. [11] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall punish the world for its evil, and the wrong for their crookedness, and shall put an end to the arrogance of the proud, and lay low the pride of the ruthless.</dq> [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall make mortal man scarcer than fine gold, and mankind scarcer than the gold of Ophir.</dq> [13] <dq>“So <dn>I</dn> shall make the heavens tremble, and the earth shall shake from her place, in the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts and in the day of the heat of <dn>His</dn> displeasure.</dq>

readings.title: The Scattering of the Arrogant
readings.subtitle: The dissolution of systemic harmony yields absolute vulnerability.
readings.text: [Isaiah 13:14] <dq>“And it shall be as the hunted gazelle, and as a sheep that no man takes up – every man turns to his own people, and everyone flees to his own land.</dq> [15] <dq>“Whoever is found is thrust through, and everyone taken falls by the sword.</dq> [16] <dq>“And their children are dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses plundered and their wives ravished.</dq>

readings.title: The Terminal State of Baḇel
readings.subtitle: The geographic crucible of confusion reduced to an unsalvageable wasteland.
readings.text: [Isaiah 13:17] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am stirring up the Medes against them, who do not regard silver, and as for gold, they do not delight in it.</dq> [18] <dq>“And bows dash the young to pieces, and they have no compassion on the fruit of the womb, their eye spares no children.</dq> [19] <dq>“And Baḇel, the splendour of reigns, the comeliness of the pride of the Kasdim, shall be as when <dn>Elohim</dn> overthrew Seḏom and Amorah.</dq> [20] <dq>“She shall never be inhabited, nor be settled from generation to generation; nor shall the Araḇian pitch tents there, nor shepherds rest their flocks there.</dq> [21] <dq>“But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there, and their houses shall be filled with owls. And ostriches shall dwell there, and wild goats frolic there.</dq> [22] <dq>“And hyenas shall cry in their citadels, and jackals in their pleasant palaces. And her time is near to come, and her days are not drawn out.”</dq>

readings.title: The Restoration of Yisra’ěl
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH reestablishes His authoritative family and reverses the captivity.
readings.text: [Isaiah 14:1] Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has compassion on Ya‛aqoḇ, and shall again choose Yisra’ěl, and give them rest in their own land. And the strangers shall join them, and they shall cling to the house of Ya‛aqoḇ. [2] And peoples shall take them and bring them to their own place. And the house of Yisra’ěl shall possess them for servants and female servants in the land of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they shall make captives of their captors, and rule over their oppressors.

readings.title: A Proverb Against the Architect of Confusion
readings.subtitle: The earthly administrators of the penal system are brought low to She'ol.
readings.text: [Isaiah 14:3] And it shall be, in the day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gives you rest from your sorrow, and from your trouble and the hard service in which you were made to serve, [4] that you shall take up this proverb against the sovereign of Baḇel, and say, “How the oppressor has ceased, the gold-gatherer ceased! [5] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has broken the staff of the wrong, the sceptre of the rulers, [6] he who struck the people in wrath with ceaseless blows, he who ruled the nations in displeasure, is persecuted and no one restrains. [7] “All the earth is at rest and at peace, they shall break forth into singing. [8] “Even the cypress trees rejoice over you, and the cedars of Leḇanon, saying, ‘Since you were cut down, no woodcutter has come up against us.’ [9] “She’ol from beneath is excited about you, to meet you at your coming; it stirs up the dead for you, all the chief ones of the earth; it has raised up from their thrones all the sovereigns of the nations. [10] “All of them respond and say to you, ‘Have you also become as weak as we? Have you become like us? [11] Your arrogance has been brought down to She’ol, and the sound of your stringed instruments; the maggot is spread under you, and worms cover you.’

readings.title: The Fall of the Left Arm
readings.subtitle: Hělěl’s rebellion to usurp the singular Creator results in his ultimate demotion.
readings.text: [Isaiah 14:12] “How you have fallen from the heavens, O Hělěl, son of the morning! You have been cut down to the ground, you who laid low the nations! [13] “For you have said in your heart, ‘Let me go up to the heavens, let me raise my throne above the stars of <dn>Ěl</dn>, and let me sit in the mount of appointment on the sides of the north; [14] let me go up above the heights of the clouds, let me be like the Most High.’ [15] “But you are brought down to She’ol, to the sides of the pit.

readings.title: The World Ponders the Fallen Adversary
readings.subtitle: The ultimate fate of the one who stripped the earth of its functional harmony.
readings.text: [Isaiah 14:16] “Those who see you stare at you, and ponder over you, saying, ‘Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook reigns, [17] who made the world as a wilderness and destroyed its cities, who would not open the house of his prisoners?’ [18] “All the sovereigns of the nations, all of them, were laid in esteem, everyone in his own house; [19] but you have been thrown from your burial-site like an abominable branch, like the garment of those who are killed, thrust through with a sword, who go down to the stones of the pit, like a trampled corpse. [20] “You are not joined with them in the burial-place, for you have destroyed your land and killed your people. Let the seed of evil-doers never be mentioned.

readings.title: The Sweeping of Baḇel
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH eradicates the seed of the adversary's system.
readings.text: [Isaiah 14:21] “Prepare his children for slaughter, because of the crookedness of their fathers, lest they rise up and possess the land, and fill the face of the world with cities.” [22] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall rise up against them,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“and shall cut off from Baḇel the name and remnant, and offspring and descendant,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [23] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make it a possession for the porcupine, and marshes of muddy water; and shall sweep it with the broom of destruction,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.

readings.title: The Unbreakable Counsel of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The structural guarantee of Ashshur's defeat on the mountains of Yisra’ěl.
readings.text: [Isaiah 14:24] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts has sworn, saying, <dq>“Truly, as <dn>I</dn> have planned, so shall it be; and as <dn>I</dn> have purposed, so it stands:</dq> [25] <dq>“To break Ashshur in <dn>My</dn> land, and tread him down on <dn>My</dn> mountains. And his yoke shall be removed from them, and his burden removed from their shoulders.</dq> [26] <dq>“This is the counsel that is counselled for all the earth, and this is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.</dq> [27] <dq>“For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts has counselled, and who annuls it? And <dn>His</dn> hand that is stretched out, who turns it back?”</dq>

readings.title: Oracle Against Philistia
readings.subtitle: Tsiyon remains the founded refuge against the northern smoke.
readings.text: [Isaiah 14:28] This is the message which came in the year that Sovereign Aḥaz died: [29] <dq>“Do not rejoice, all you of Philistia, that the rod that struck you is broken; for out of the serpent’s roots comes forth an adder, and its offspring is a fiery flying serpent.</dq> [30] <dq>“And the first-born of the poor shall feed, and the needy lie down in safety. And <dn>I</dn> shall kill your roots with scarcity of food, and it shall kill your remnant.</dq> [31] <dq>“Howl, O gate! Cry, O city! Melt away, all you of Philistia! For smoke shall come from the north, and there is no stranger in his ranks.”</dq> [32] And what does one answer the messengers of a nation? <dq>“That <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has founded Tsiyon, and the poor of <dn>His</dn> people take refuge in it.”</dq>

readings.title: The Silencing of Mo’aḇ
readings.subtitle: A sudden devastation brings bitter weeping and baldness.
readings.text: [Isaiah 15:1] The message concerning Mo’aḇ. Because in the night Ar of Mo’aḇ was laid waste, was silenced! Because in the night Qir of Mo’aḇ was laid waste, was silenced! [2] He has gone up to the house and Diḇon, to the high places to weep. Mo’aḇ is wailing over Neḇo and over Měyḏeḇa; on all their heads is baldness, and every beard is cut off. [3] In their streets they shall put on sackcloth; on the tops of their houses and in their streets everyone wails, weeping bitterly. [4] And Ḥeshbon and El‛alěh cry out, their voice shall be heard as far as Yahats. Therefore the armed ones of Mo’aḇ shout; his being shall tremble within him.

readings.title: The Flight of the Fugitives
readings.subtitle: The physical environment withers as Mo’aḇ flees the coming lion.
readings.text: [Isaiah 15:5] My own heart is toward Mo’aḇ; her fugitives cry unto Tso‛ar, like a three-year-old heifer. For by the ascent of Luḥith they go up with weeping; for in the way of Ḥoronayim they raise a cry of destruction. [6] For the waters of Nimrim are wastes, for the green grass has withered away; the grass fails, there is no greenness. [7] Therefore the wealth, acquired and stored up, they take away to the wadi of the Willows. [8] For the cry has gone all around the borders of Mo’aḇ, its wailing to Eḡlayim and its wailing to Be’ěr Ělim. [9] <dq>“For the waters of Dimon shall be filled with blood; for <dn>I</dn> shall bring more upon Dimon, lions upon him who escapes from Mo’aḇ, and on the remnant of the land.”</dq>

readings.title: The Righteous Tent of Daviḏ
readings.subtitle: A prophetic glimpse into the restorative, premial throne established in truth.
readings.text: [Isaiah 16:1] Send a lamb to the ruler of the land, from Sela to the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Tsiyon. [2] And it shall be, like a wandering bird, a nest thrown out, so are the daughters of Mo’aḇ at the fords of Arnon. [3] “Bring counsel, execute judgment; make your shadow like the night in the middle of the day; hide the outcasts, do not betray him who escapes. [4] <dq>“Let <dn>My</dn> outcasts dwell with you, O Mo’aḇ; be a shelter to them from the face of the ravager. For the oppressor has met his end, destruction has ceased, those trampling down have perished from the land.</dq> [5] <dq>“And in loving-commitment the throne shall be established. And One shall sit on it in truth, in the Tent of Daviḏ, judging and seeking right-ruling, and speeding righteousness.”</dq>

readings.title: The Arrogance and Languishing of Mo’aḇ
readings.subtitle: Empty boastings yield a withered harvest and silenced vineyards.
readings.text: [Isaiah 16:6] We have heard of the pride of Mo’aḇ – very proud – of his pride, his arrogance and his rage. His boastings are not true. [7] So Mo’aḇ wails for Mo’aḇ, everyone wails. For the raisin-cakes of Qir Ḥareseth they moan. They are utterly smitten. [8] For the fields of Ḥeshbon languish – the vine of Siḇmah. The masters of the nations have broken down its choice plants, which have reached to Ya‛zěr and wandered through the wilderness. Her branches are stretched out, they are gone over the sea. [9] Therefore I bewail the vine of Siḇmah, with the weeping of Ya‛zěr. I water you with my tears, O Ḥeshbon and El‛alěh, for acclamation has fallen over your summer fruit and your harvest. [10] Gladness is taken away, and joy from the orchard; in the vineyards there is no singing, nor shouting; No treaders tread out wine in their presses; I have made their acclamation cease. [11] Therefore my inward parts sound like a lyre for Mo’aḇ, and my inner being for Qir Ḥeres. [12] And it shall be, when it is seen that Mo’aḇ has wearied herself on the high place, that she shall come to her set-apart place to pray, but not be able.

readings.title: The Three-Year Verdict
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH issues a strictly timed decree against the esteem of Mo’aḇ.
readings.text: [Isaiah 16:13] This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken concerning Mo’aḇ since that time. [14] But now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken, saying, <dq>“Within three years, as the years of a hired man, the esteem of Mo’aḇ is to be despised with all its great throng, and the remnant be few, small and weak.”</dq>
